questions.heading: A Disjunction Written as Big-M Switches Each Disjunct With Its Own Binary
questions.stem: Jobs A (4 months) and B (6 months) share an outage in a 10-month season, with starts s_A in [0, 6] and s_B in [0, 4]. The row for 'A before B' is s_A + 4 <= s_B + M(1 - y). What is the smallest M the bounds justify?

options.text: M = 10, with s_A at 6 and s_B at 0
options.says: Right: the most s_A + 4 - s_B can be is 6 + 4 - 0.

options.text: M = 4, since only A's own work must always fit
options.says: M covers the largest value of s_A + 4 - s_B over the bounds, which is 10.

options.text: M = 16, the season plus B's whole duration
options.says: B's duration is not in this row; the bound rule gives 10.

options.text: M = 6, A's latest start, since s_B is never negative
options.says: The row's left side also adds A's 4 months: 6 + 4 - 0 = 10.

questions.heading: The Hull Gives Each Disjunct Its Own Copy of the Variables
questions.stem: Two jobs are ordered with the hull formulation, and in the LP relaxation the switch y ('i goes first') comes out at 0.4. What are the LP's start values for the pair?

options.text: Any starts at all, since a fractional switch loosens both orders
options.says: That is the big-M form; in the hull each copy obeys its own order, scaled by its switch.

options.text: The starts of one whole order, since the hull keeps the switch whole
options.says: The LP relaxation lets y be a fraction; here it is 0.4.

options.text: The same starts as big-M, since both forms allow the same plans
options.says: Both allow the same whole-number plans, but their LP relaxations differ: 10 against 13.98 on the outage jobs.

options.text: A blend of the two orders' schedules, weighted by the switch
options.says: Right: the copies are each order's schedule scaled by its switch, and the starts are their sum.

questions.heading: The Hull Is Tighter but Bigger, and for One Variable a Tight Big-M Already Is the Hull
questions.stem: A pump's pressure p must lie either in [20, 40] or in [70, 90], written as two big-M rows with the tight Ms from the bounds 20 <= p <= 90. A colleague proposes the hull formulation to tighten the LP. What should you expect?

options.text: A tighter LP bound, since the hull is always tighter than big-M
options.says: For one variable over intervals the tight big-M rows are already the hull's edges.

options.text: A looser LP bound, since the hull splits p into copies
options.says: The hull is never looser; here it describes the same LP region.

options.text: The same LP bound, from a model with more variables and rows
options.says: Right: the two forms gave identical LP values on every objective, and the hull adds copies and cap rows.

options.text: An infeasible LP, since the copies need bounds that p never has
options.says: p has bounds, 20 to 90, and the copies' caps are built from them.
